I am submitting this as a supplemental statement to my CFPB complaint against CrossCountry Mortgage to document not only escrow misconduct and evidence withholding, but a complete breakdown of the regulatory framework that is supposed to protect homeowners from exactly this type of conduct.

This matter is not closed. Escrow funds were taken and disbursed without lawful justification, without verified evidence, and without compliance with federal servicing obligations. CrossCountry Mortgages attempt to label this matter closed, while treating continued demands for proof as new requests, is procedurally improper and substantively indefensible.

CrossCountry Mortgage was on notice of a bona fide dispute regarding the validity and enforceability of the HOA charge prior to and/or at the time of disbursement. Once notice exists, a mortgage servicer has independent, non-delegable duties to investigate, document, and verify the legal basis for any escrow disbursement. Those duties can not be delegated to an HOA, ignored, or replaced by a regulators refusal letter. 

To date, CrossCountry Mortgage has never identified or produced the evidence it relied upon to justify taking and disbursing escrow funds. If such evidence exists, it must be produced. If it does not exist, the disbursement was not justified.

CrossCountry Mortgage has attempted to rely on correspondence from the XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX ( XXXX  ) to justify its conduct. That reliance is improper. Even if XXXX had conducted a review, a state regulators position does not relieve a federal mortgage servicer of its independent obligations under federal law. A refusal to investigate can not substitute for compliance. 

XXXX own correspondence demonstrates that no meaningful investigation occurred. The letter does not identify what evidence was reviewed, what records were obtained, what documents were examined, or what factual findings were made. XXXX has not stated that it reviewed my recorded deed, HOA source financial records, escrow account documentation, or county recording records. 

This raises unavoidable questions that remain unanswered : What specific evidence did XXXX rely upon to justify its conclusions? 

Did XXXX obtain and review my recorded deed, and if so, where in that deed does it authorize the conduct being excused? 

If XXXX did not review the deed, how could it evaluate deed-based obligations or determine enforceability? 

Did XXXX verify whether any lien, assessment, or enforceable obligation was ever lawfully recorded with the XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX? To date, no such recording exists. 

An investigation without evidence is not an investigation. Conclusions issued without documentation are unsupported. 

XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXXXXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX program also reviewed aspects of this matter. While no formal enforcement action was taken, the VA acknowledged the validity of the concerns raised. That acknowledgment further confirms that the issues presented were real, substantiated, and required scrutiny. Yet despite that acknowledgment, no corrective action followed. 

XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXXXXXX has also declined to take action, stating that it only handles certain types of complaints. As a result, the Attorney General will not intervene, XXXX will not investigate, the HOA will not produce records, and CrossCountry Mortgage refuses to produce evidence while declaring the matter closed. 

This leaves homeowners in an impossible position. 

When every agency tasked with oversight disclaims responsibility, when no evidence is produced, when no lien exists, and when escrow funds are nevertheless taken, what is a homeowner supposed to do? 

What is the purpose of these regulatory bodies if they neither compel evidence nor enforce compliance? 

This is not a hypothetical concern. This is a live example of systemic regulatory failure that allows escrow funds to be taken without proof and without accountability. 

If XXXX Mortgage or XXXX contend that evidence exists but can not be produced, that raises serious record-retention and preservation concerns. If no evidence exists, then their conclusions are unsupported and the escrow disbursement can not be justified. Either scenario demands federal intervention. 

I respectfully request that CFPB require XXXX Mortgage to either ( 1 ) produce the specific documentary evidence relied upon to justify the escrow disbursement and to declare this matter closed, or ( 2 ) formally acknowledge that no such evidence exists and take corrective action accordingly, including reimbursement and a written compliance explanation. 

Until verified evidence is produced, this matter can not be considered resolved and will not be considered resolved until the money taken from illegally is returned.

During the statutory XXXX dispute period, the debt collectors designated dispute website XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX  was unavailable due to scheduled weekly maintenance, preventing submission of a dispute through the method provided. 

The maintenance notice states that the dispute site is unavailable every Saturday from XXXX XXXX  until Sunday at XXXX XXXX  ( Central Time ). At the point of dispute, no equally accessible alternative written dispute method was clearly provided. 

Because the debt collector designated the website as the dispute mechanism, the recurring and predictable outage materially impaired my ability to exercise my dispute rights under 15 U.S.C. 1692g and CFPB Regulation F ( 12 C.F.R. Part 1006 ). The scheduled unavailability effectively shortened the statutory dispute window and imposed a procedural barrier on a federally protected consumer right.

15 U.S.C. 1692g requires that consumers be given a meaningful opportunity to dispute debts within 30 days. Regulation F permits electronic dispute methods, but once designated, those methods must be reasonably available. A single, designated dispute channel that is regularly unavailable, without a clearly disclosed alternative, constitutes an unreasonable impediment to the exercise of statutory rights and may qualify as an unfair or unconscionable practice under 15 U.S.C. 1692f.

The dispute mechanisms recurring unavailability appears to be a systemic compliance issue rather than an isolated outage. Because the dispute website is unavailable for a predictable, recurring period each week, the designated dispute channel is not continuously available during the statutory 30-day dispute period. This recurring blackout materially reduces the practical time available to exercise dispute rights and places control over access to a federally protected right in the hands of the debt collector, contrary to the requirements of 15 U.S.C. 1692g and CFPB Regulation F. 

That said, I will be preserving my dispute of this debt by submitting it tomorrow.

Under 26 U.S.C. 6050P and Treasury Regulation 26 C.F.R. 1.6050P-1, a creditor is required to file and furnish IRS Form 1099-C when {$600.00} or more of debt is canceled or discharged following an identifiable cancellation event. In this case : The account reflects a charge-off / write-off The amount exceeds the {$600.00} statutory threshold The account continues to report as past due No IRS Form 1099-C has been issued or provided A creditor can not lawfully treat a debt as written off while simultaneously avoiding mandatory federal tax reporting obligations. If the debt was canceled, BMO Bank N.A . is legally required to issue Form 1099-C. If the debt was not canceled, reporting it as a charge-off/write-off is materially misleading. Either position results in inaccurate credit reporting. Improper and Misleading Charge-Off / Delinquency Reporting BMO Bank N.A . is continuing to report this account as : Charged off Written off Past due These reporting positions are legally and factually inconsistent. A debt that has been charged off and written off can not simultaneously remain an active delinquent obligation without clear disclosure of legal enforceability. This creates a false impression of ongoing liability and materially misrepresents the accounts true status. Fair Credit Reporting Act ( FCRA ) Violations BMO Bank N.A.s reporting violates the Fair Credit Reporting Act, including but not limited to : 15 U.S.C. 1681s-2 ( a ) ( 1 ) ( A ) Furnishing information that is inaccurate or materially misleading 15 U.S.C. 1681e ( b ) Failure to maintain reasonable procedures to ensure maximum possible accuracy 15 U.S.C. 1681s-2 ( b ) Failure to conduct a reasonable investigation into the legal and accounting status of the debt Continuing to report a charge-off while failing to comply with federal tax reporting requirements constitutes systemic misrepresentation. Demand for Relief I hereby demand that BMO Bank N.A . take the following corrective action : Immediately issue IRS Form 1099-C reflecting cancellation of the charged-off debt ; Delete this tradeline from all consumer reporting agencies ( XXXX XXXX XXXX ) due to inaccurate and misleading reporting. Absent compliance, continued reporting constitutes willful noncompliance with federal law. This complaint is being submitted to the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau ( CFPB ) for regulatory review and enforcement. Please provide a written response within the CFPB-mandated response timeframe. Sincerely,

Company : Credit Saint, LLC Product Type : Credit repair services Issue Type : Billing / fees charged before services completed Desired Resolution : Refund of fees charged during ongoing investigations ; review of billing practices for compliance Complaint Narrative I am submitting this complaint regarding Credit Saint, LLCs billing practices for credit repair services.

Credit Saint bills a recurring monthly fee approximately every 30 days. However, the credit bureau investigations associated with the disputes initiated by Credit Saint routinely remain open for up to 45 days, as permitted under the Fair Credit Reporting Act. 

As a result, I am charged a monthly fee while the investigations are still legally ongoing and unresolved. At the time of billing, no investigation results have been received, no outcomes have been delivered, and no consumer-verifiable results exist. The service for which I am billed is therefore incomplete at the time the fee is charged. 

This practice effectively constitutes the collection of a fee before services are fully rendered. 

The CFPB has previously addressed this issue in its enforcement action against XXXX XXXX / XXXX, where the Bureau and the federal court rejected the argument that preparatory or administrative work ( such as submitting disputes or awaiting bureau responses ) constitutes completion of credit repair services. In that case, the CFPB determined that charging consumers before results were achieved violated federal consumer protection laws, regardless of how the fees were labeled ( e.g., monthly or service fees ). 

In my case, Credit Saints billing cycle overlaps unresolved investigations, meaning consumers are charged while legally required investigations are still pending and before the consumer can assess whether any service outcome has been achieved. 

This practice leaves consumers without transparency, without results, and without the ability to verify that services have been completed before payment is taken. 

I respectfully request that the CFPB review Credit Saints billing practices for compliance with federal consumer protection standards and require appropriate remediation, including refunds of fees charged during periods when investigations were still ongoing. 

Credit Saint charged me {$99.00} before investigations were completed. Then attempted another charge after 30 days, again before the investigation process was completed, which appears inconsistent with the Credit Repair Organizations Act ( CROA ) and CFPB guidance prohibiting advance fees prior to the completion of promised services. 

I have since disputed the charge with my credit card issuer.

Consumer complaint narrative:
I am filing this complaint regarding Capital Ones handling of a billing dispute on my credit card account. Capital One initially issued a temporary credit while investigating the dispute, but later reversed that credit based solely on the merchants response.

The merchant was unreachable despite multiple attempts to contact them directly. Capital One did not take into account the merchants failure to respond to me or the lack of a meaningful opportunity to resolve the issue outside of the dispute process.

Capital One relied exclusively on the merchants assertion of a non-refundable policy without demonstrating that the policy was clearly disclosed, fairly applied, or independently verified. I was not provided sufficient documentation showing that Capital One conducted a reasonable investigation beyond accepting the merchants claims at face value.

As a result, the charge was reapplied to my account despite unresolved concerns regarding the accuracy and fairness of the charge, causing financial harm.

I believe Capital One failed to conduct a reasonable investigation as required under the Fair Credit Billing Act. The investigation did not adequately consider the merchants lack of responsiveness or verify whether the charge was properly applied and handled in accordance with consumer protections.

Based on Capital Ones response, the merchant asserted to Capital One that a refund was issued to an alternate form of payment. This assertion is inaccurate. The charge was made using a virtual card number that is directly linked to the same underlying Capital One credit card account as the physical card. A refund issued to the virtual card would necessarily post to the same account.

No refund was ever received or posted to the account. Capital One did not provide documentation showing that a refund was processed, traced, or reconciled to the account, nor did they verify the merchants claim that funds were returned to an alternate payment method.

By accepting the merchants statement without proof of a completed refund to the account, Capital One failed to conduct a reasonable investigation and improperly relied on an unverified merchant assertion.

Company : Nelnet Product : Federal Student Loan Servicing Issue Type : Incorrect balance / Interest accrual / Failure to investigate Complaint Type : Unfair and deceptive acts or practices ( UDAAP ) Complaint Summary I was incarcerated for approximately six ( 6 ) years. During this documented period, Nelnet knowingly allowed interest to accrue and my loan balance to increase, and later refused to correct the account after receiving notice and documentation. This constitutes unfair servicing conduct under CFPB standards.

Detailed Description I was incarcerated for approximately six years and therefore physically unable to manage, service, or meaningfully interact with my student loan account during that time.

Despite this, Nelnet : Allowed interest to accrue automatically throughout my incarceration Permitted balance growth that I could not prevent Retained full control over interest mechanics while I had no practical ability to avoid the harm After my release, I notified Nelnet of my incarceration and requested review and correction. Rather than conducting a meaningful investigation, Nelnet issued a boilerplate denial through its Ombudsman, failed to address the substance of the issue, and refused to correct the improperly accrued interest.

Not Reasonably Avoidable Incarceration eliminated my ability to manage the account. Nelnet controlled interest accrual entirely.

No Countervailing Benefit There is no consumer or market benefit to allowing interest to accrue against an incarcerated borrower who can not act.

Additionally, Nelnets failure to investigate after notice elevates this from error to unfair servicing practice.

Relief Requested I am requesting that Nelnet be required to : Remove and credit all interest accrued during my incarceration Recalculate my account balance with a written itemization Refund or credit any improper charges Provide a written explanation of its review methodology Confirm corrected servicing going forward Supporting Documentation I am prepared to provide : Proof of incarceration dates Account statements showing interest accrual Prior complaints and correspondence Ombudsman denial demonstrating failure to investigate Resolution Requested Correction of account balance and interest, written explanation, and assurance of compliant servicing.

Based on this guidance, I relied on the XX/XX/XXXX payment date and scheduled payment accordingly. 

Despite these assurances, my account was placed with a third-party collection agency ( XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XX/XX/XXXX, prior to the XX/XX/XXXX date I had been instructed to rely upon. 

Upon receiving communication from the collection agency, I immediately contacted Upstart to ask about the discrepancy. During that call, I was told that Upstart was no longer handling my account, that I would need to deal exclusively with the third-party agency, and that all payments must go through the collection agency from that point forward. I was not offered the option to resolve the account directly through Upstart, despite still being within the date I was told would preserve my standing. 

Upstart later stated in writing that my contract remained with them and that payment through the Upstart dashboard was still available. This directly contradicts the instructions I was given at the time, when I was explicitly redirected away from Upstart and refused the ability to make payment through them.

Regulation X 1024.30 ( d ) reads as follows : ( d ) Successors in interest. A confirmed successor in interest shall be considered a borrower for purposes of 1024.17 and this subpart.

It happens that 12 CFR 1024.17 deals specifically with Escrow Accounts and the servicing of Escrow accounts by lenders.

CFPBs own commentary on Regulation X ( RESPA servicing rules ) reads as follows : 30 ( d ) Successors in interest.

1. Treatment of confirmed successors in interest. Under 1024.30 ( d ), a confirmed successor in interest must be considered a borrower for purposes of this subpart and 1024.17, regardless of whether the successor in interest assumes the mortgage loan obligation under State law. For example, if a servicer receives a loss mitigation application from a confirmed successor in interest, the servicer must review and evaluate the application and notify the confirmed successor in interest in accordance with the procedures set forth in 1024.41 if the property is the confirmed successor in interest 's principal residence and the procedures set forth in 1024.41 are otherwise applicable. Treatment of a confirmed successor in interest as a borrower for purposes of this subpart and 1024.17 does not affect whether the confirmed successor in interest is subject to the contractual obligations of the mortgage loan agreement, which is determined by applicable State law. 2Communications in compliance with this part to a confirmed successor in interest as defined in 1024.31 do not violate section 805 ( b ) of the Fair Debt Collection Practices Act ( FDCPA ) because consumer for purposes of FDCPA section 805 includes any person who meets the definition in this part of confirmed successor in interest.

Large mortgage lenders know that there are many cases involving Successors in Interest where an expensive and lengthy probate process is neither required nor applicable. They furthermore know that there are states where Small Estate Affidavits can not be obtained. Therefore demands for probate documents or Small Estate Affidavits should be considered mechanisms to obstruct and delay ( in many cases, permanently ) the payment of funds due to Successors under Regulation X.

I furthermore submit that Wells Fargo Home Mortgage should be investigated not only in my case but in the cases of other Successors in Interest as well, as my own personal research has produced anecdotal evidence that lenders like Wells Fargo Home Mortgage and other large lenders are violating the requirements of Regulation X {$1000.00} ( d ) systematically.

Given that Wells Fargo Home Mortgage is obligated under this provision to treat me effectively as the borrower with regard to all escrow servicing matters, they have yet to directly address why they have not done so as required by this provision.

If Wells Fargo Home Mortgage is claiming that it is not in violation of Regulation X {$1000.00} ( d ) in my case - and in the case of any Successors in Interest in my situation- it needs to make clear to CFPB and the public its legal justification for taking this position. Consumer complaint narrative:

TD Bank provided no transaction-level evidence demonstrating that I initiated, approved, or authenticated the disputed charges. After identifying additional unauthorized charges, I filed another fraud claim, which was also denied on the same unsupported basis. 

During the investigation, TD Bank did not issue a provisional or temporary credit for the disputed transactions. As a result, interest, fees, adverse credit reporting, and account closure actions were allowed to occur while the fraud claim remained unresolved. Many credit card issuers provide temporary credits during fraud investigations specifically to prevent consumer harm. TD Banks failure to do so materially worsened the impact of the disputed transactions and compounded the resulting harm. 

I subsequently filed a police report documenting suspected theft and submitted it to TD Bank in support of an open fraud claim ( Claim No. XXXX, opened XX/XX/XXXX ). Despite receipt of the police report, TD Bank again denied the fraud claim without producing affirmative proof of authorization or reconciling the contradiction between its own fraud alert and its denial determination. 

While the fraud dispute remained unresolved, TD Bank reported the account as past due to credit bureaus and subsequently closed the account based on non-payment of the disputed fraudulent balance. This action caused significant and avoidable credit harm arising directly from TD Banks failure to conduct a reasonable and lawful investigation. 

In addition to the improper handling of the disputed business credit card account, TD Bank reduced the credit limit on my personal TD Bank credit account, even though the disputed transactions were associated with a separate business account. This action was taken while the fraud dispute remained unresolved.

TD Banks decision to reduce my personal credit limit appears to be based on the unresolved disputed balance rather than any change in my personal creditworthiness. This collateral adverse action directly harmed my personal credit utilization, available credit, and credit score, extending the impact of TD Banks flawed fraud determination beyond the business account under dispute.

Penalizing a consumers personal credit profile based on disputed transactions on a separate business account, without substantiating authorization or resolving the fraud investigation constitutes unfair and disproportionate treatment and magnifies consumer harm caused by the original investigative failure.

Instead, they continued collection-style communications and refused to address insolvency or elect any remedy under the contract, such as termination or removal of their owned equipment.

A complaint regarding this conduct has also been filed with the Texas Attorney General, Consumer Protection Division ( Complaint No. XXXX ). 

I am requesting CFPB review of the servicers post-death debt collection practices and failure to properly handle this account in a probate-appropriate manner.

After I vacated the unit, XXXX XXXX XXXX issued a move-out statement claiming I owed a balance. I contacted the landlord to request documentation supporting the charges. I was informed that because the account had been sent to collections, it was no longer their responsibility to provide proof or justification of the charges. I then sent a written dispute and request for validation to National Credit Systems, which they received on XX/XX/year>. Despite receiving my dispute, National Credit Systems did not respond, did not provide validation, and continued reporting the debt to the credit bureaus.

I am requesting intervention because this matter involves inaccurate credit reporting, failure to properly validate a disputed debt, and the continued reporting of an alleged obligation that is not supported by complete or reliable documentation. PRELIMINARY STATEMENT OF GOOD FAITH Before detailing the specific regulatory violations, the Complainant wishes to state for the record that this filing is submitted in good faith to preserve, rather than dissolve, the banking relationship. The Complainant values his membership with Navy Federal Credit Union and has no desire or intent to close these accounts. This action is taken solely to compel the correction of specific billing errors and to ensure institutional adherence to federal consumer protection laws which, to date, have not been addressed through standard customer service channels. 



SUMMARY I am filing this formal complaint against Navy Federal Credit Union ( NFCU ) due to their failure to adhere to federal billing regulations, improper payment allocation under the Truth in Lending Act ( TILA ), and systemic customer service failures that resulted in compounding fees and financial harm. Despite multiple attempts to resolve these matters directly, NFCU has provided conflicting information and failed to reconcile clear mathematical errors on my accounts. 




STATEMENT OF FACTS PART A : Payment Allocation & Regulation Z Dispute ( Visa Account # XXXX ) On XX/XX/year>, I made a payment significantly in excess of the minimum required on my CashRewards Visa. Under 12 CFR 1026.53 ( a ) ( Regulation Z ), payments exceeding the minimum must be applied to the balance with the highest APR first ( in this case, the Cash Advance balance ). 
The Issue : NFCU misapplied these funds, leaving the high-interest Cash Advance balance active while applying funds to lower-APR purchase balances.

The Harm : This has caused {$680.00} to continue accruing interest improperly. When I contacted support, I was told interest would accrue until the entire card was zeroa statement that directly contradicts federal " Highest APR First '' allocation mandates. 
PART B : Billing Error & Over-Limit Dispute ( Visa Account # XXXX ) On XX/XX/year>, a charge of {$630.00} from the XXXX XXXX Treasurer was processed. 
The Issue : The charge was erroneously duplicated or mishandled. While a " reversal '' appeared, the reversal amount ( {$680.00} ) did not match the original charge. 
The Harm : Because of this discrepancy, my account now reflects an inflated balance of XXXX XXXXexceeding my {$1500.00} limit. I am being charged interest and potentially over-limit fees on a balance that exists solely due to NFCU 's inability to reconcile a mathematical error. 


PART C : Business Account Mismanagement & Fee Compounding ( Business Account # XXXX ) I experienced a technical issue with my PIN at an ATM. 
The Issue : After several failed attempts resulting in {$1.00} fees, I contacted NFCU for immediate assistance to reset the PIN and prevent further fees. The first representative failed to provide the necessary support. 
The Harm : Due to the lack of effective support, I made subsequent attempts that accrued further fees. While a second representative eventually assisted, the initial negligence caused unnecessary financial depletion and operational disruption to my business, XXXX XXXX XXXX.

PHHs issuance of a foreclosure-intent notice after receipt of a complete loss mitigation application constitutes impermissible dual tracking.

Additionally, Wells Fargo instructed me to obtain payoff statements for other debts and to preserve balances during payoff periods, actions that are standard within refinance workflows. Discover Bank is furnishing inaccurate and misleading credit information by reporting current late payments and delinquency on a closed account that incurred unauthorized charges while I was incarcerated. Discover was formally notified of my incarceration and the fraud, yet continues to report the account as late rather than suppressing, correcting, or removing the derogatory information.yhe account was also sold to a collection agency which is also reporting to my credit as well This conduct violates the Fair Credit Reporting Act ( FCRA ) and applicable furnisher duties, and reflects a failure to conduct a reasonable investigation after notice of fraud and identity-related misuse.

I notified Discover Bank of my incarceration and that the charges were fraudulent.

Legal Violations 1. Fair Credit Reporting Act 15 U.S.C. 1681s-2 ( a ) & ( b ) Discover, as a furnisher, is prohibited from reporting information it knows or has reasonable cause to believe is inaccurate. Once notified of a dispute, Discover is required to : Conduct a reasonable investigation Review all relevant information Correct or delete inaccurate information Reporting current late payments arising from fraudulent charges incurred while the consumer was incarcerated is inherently inaccurate and misleading.

Continuing to report delinquency without addressing the impossibility of consumer authorization during incarceration is per se unreasonable. 

3. Materially Misleading Reporting ( Regulation V, 12 C.F.R. 1022 ) Even if Discover claims the balance exists, reporting current lates without accounting for fraud and incarceration is materially misleading, which is prohibited under Regulation V.

4. Identity Theft/ Fraud Protections ( 15 U.S.C. 1681c-2 ) Charges incurred while the consumer is incarcerated constitute identity-related fraud or unauthorized use. Discover failed to appropriately block or correct reporting after notice. 



Harm Caused Ongoing credit score suppression due to inaccurately reported current delinquencies Increased risk-based pricing, denial of credit, and financial harm Continued reputational harm due to false credit data Requested Resolution I respectfully request that the CFPB require Discover Bank to : 1. Immediately delete all late payments and derogatory marks associated with the disputed period 2. Remove or correct the tradeline to reflect fraud/unauthorized activity 3. Cease reporting any delinquency related to charges incurred during my incarceration 4. Provide written confirmation of corrections to all credit reporting agencies 5. Verification and validation are distinct legal concepts, and I demand that you provide both.

Verification is the process of confirming whether I actually owe the debt, as referenced in Chaudhry v. Gallerizzo, 174 F.3d 394 ( 4th Cir. 1999 ). According to Blacks Law Dictionary, verification is defined as an averment that the party pleading is ready to establish the truth of what he has set forth. The examination of a writing for the purpose of ascertaining its truth ; or a certificate or affidavit that it is true. In McDonald v. Rosengarten, 134 Ill. 126, 25 N.E. ( 1890 ), the court explained that verification involves the " confirmation of the correctness, truth, or authenticity of a pleading, account, or other paper, by an affidavit, oath, or deposition. '' Other courts, such as in Summerfield v. Phoenix Assur. Co. ( C. C. ) 65 Fed. 296 ( 1922 ) and Patterson v. Brooklyn, 6 App. Div. 127, 40 N.Y. Supp. 581 ( 1898 ), have reiterated this legal principle.

Therefore, I request the following : Proof that I am legally responsible for the debt in question.

A verified statement of the original creditor and the contract or agreement that created the debt.

Validation is necessary to confirm the legitimacy of this debt before any further action can be taken, as referenced in Spears v. Brennan, 745 N.E. 2d 862 Ind. App. ( 2001 ). Black 's Law Dictionary defines validation as assessing an action to determine it is complete, correct, implemented, and delivering the correct outcome. XXXX defines it as to check or prove the validity or accuracy of something, and XXXX explains it as to show the existence or truth of, by evidence. 

To this end, I am requesting that you provide : Validation of the debt, including a breakdown of how the amount was calculated, itemizing any interest, fees, or charges added to the original balance.

I am submitting this complaint regarding unauthorized withdrawals from my savings account by a third-party financial app/company ( Albert ). 

Funds were withdrawn from my savings account over an extended period of time without my authorization. When I contacted the company, I repeatedly requested documentation showing where I authorized the creation of the account, activation of any plan, or recurring withdrawals. The company was unable or unwilling to produce any proof of authorization. 

Instead of providing documentation or full restitution, the company offered partial refunds described as courtesy refunds, which increased incrementally when I objected. This behavior suggests acknowledgment of unauthorized withdrawals while attempting to cap liability. 

During the correspondence, I consistently stated that I did not authorize the withdrawals. I did not allege identity theft or third-party fraud. Despite this, the company repeatedly mischaracterized my statements by asserting that I claimed the account was fraudulently created by someone else using my identity. This framing was inaccurate and was used to justify refusing refunds. 

The company ultimately marked the account as fraudulent unilaterally and stated that, due to this designation, it could not issue refunds, directing me instead to dispute the charges with my bank. This position is contradictory : the company acknowledged the absence of authorization but refused restitution for funds already withdrawn. 

In summary, this complaint concerns : Unauthorized withdrawals from a savings account Failure to provide proof of authorization Refusal to provide full restitution Mischaracterization of consumer statements Shifting responsibility to the bank after acknowledging lack of authorization I am requesting regulatory review of these practices and assistance in obtaining full restitution for all unauthorized withdrawals.

Allowing transactions from a merchant after a customer has explicitly requested a block constitutes improper handling of disputed charges and raises concerns regarding Discovers compliance with its obligations under the Fair Credit Billing Act ( 15 U.S.C. 1666 ) and Regulation Z ( 12 C.F.R. 1026.13 ).

Under the Fair Credit Billing Act ( FCBA ), creditors are required to complete a billing dispute investigation and provide written notice of the results within XXXX  days, or XXXX billing cycles, whichever is shorter : 15 U.S.C. 1666 ( a ) requires the creditor to investigate and either correct the account or explain why the charge is valid.

2. Require Discover to provide the written investigation results and supporting documentation, or remove the disputed charges.

3. Correct my account balance and reverse all interest and fees assessed on the disputed amounts.

Company : Global Lending Services LLC Account : Global Lending Services account ending in XXXX State : Florida I am filing this complaint against Global Lending Services LLC for willful violations of the Fair Credit Reporting Act ( FCRA ), the Fair Debt Collection Practices Act ( FDCPA ), and Floridas Uniform Commercial Code arising from unlawful credit reporting and an invalid repossession deficiency claim. 

The vehicle securing this account was voluntarily surrendered. Global Lending Services disposed of the collateral and now reports this account as a charged-off repossession with a remaining balance. This reporting is materially false, misleading, and unsupported by legally required proof.

Global Lending Services has provided only a post-sale notice, which is legally insufficient under Fla. Stat. 679. To lawfully claim or report a deficiency, Global Lending Services must demonstrate strict compliance with all statutory and contractual requirements. To date, it has failed to produce verification of the following mandatory elements : Repossession & Disposition Compliance Proof of a legally compliant pre-sale notice, including the exact date sent, method of delivery, and address used Proof the pre-sale notice contained all required statutory disclosures Proof identifying the exact date, location, and method of sale Proof whether the disposition was public or private Proof of the commercial reasonableness of the sale, including fair market valuation, auction records, and comparable sales data Collateral Valuation & Sale Proceeds Proof explaining how the sale price was determined Proof the vehicle was not sold at a wholesale or insider discount Proof of odometer condition, vehicle condition report, and reconditioning adjustments Deficiency Balance & Accounting Proof of the original principal balance at the time of surrender Proof of all payments credited prior to charge-off Proof of how interest was calculated and whether interest accrued post-repossession Proof itemizing each alleged repossession, storage, auction, transport, and legal fee with invoices and vendor identification Ancillary Products & Credits Proof of GAP cancellation , refund calculation, and date applied Proof of cancellation or refund of any service contracts or extended warranties Proof that all refundable products were applied to reduce the balance Right to Collect & Furnish Proof of contractual authority to pursue a deficiency after voluntary surrender Proof of legal standing to collect the alleged balance Proof of compliance with FDCPA validation requirements prior to collection activity Under Florida law , failure to strictly comply with any repossession or disposition requirement bars enforcement of a deficiency balance. An unenforceable deficiency is not legally reportable under the FCRA. 

Despite lacking the ability to substantiate these required elements, Global Lending Services continues to willfully : Furnish inaccurate and misleading credit information Report a balance that is not capable of verification Mischaracterize the account status as a charged-off repossession Omit the voluntary surrender designation Engage in ongoing collection activity through calls and text messages without lawful validation This conduct constitutes reckless and knowing noncompliance with federal and state law and exposes Global Lending Services to liability for statutory, actual, and punitive damages. 

I am demanding that the CFPB require Global Lending Services LLC to : Immediately delete this account from all consumer reporting agencies Immediately cease all collection activity related to this alleged deficiency Provide written confirmation that the account has been permanently removed and closed with a zero balance Any continued reporting or collection activity without full, documented legal substantiation will constitute willful noncompliance and will be preserved as evidence for further regulatory and legal action.

Internal Policy Breaches : Most banks have specific, mandatory training programs and certification processes for employees handling business accounts to ensure consistency and compliance with internal protocols and regulatory requirements. 

Customer Due Diligence ( CDD ) Failures : Proper CDD for businesses is critical to assess risk correctly. A lack of training could lead to improper risk profiling or incomplete documentation. 

Fair Banking Concerns : Incorrect account opening procedures could also lead to inconsistent treatment of business customers, which might raise fair banking practice issues. Which in this case it has. 

This was discriminatory.

Consumer complaint narrative: To Whom It May Concern, I am submitting this formal complaint regarding an improperly reported collection account furnished by Southwest Recovery Services, which is reporting a collection tradeline without providing legally sufficient proof that it has the authority to collect or furnish information for this account. This conduct violates the Fair Credit Reporting Act ( 15 U.S.C. 1681 et seq. ) and applicable federal standards governing third-party debt collectors. Account Information Collection Agency : Southwest Recovery Services Account Number : XXXXXXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX Original Creditor : XXXX XXXX Amount Allegedly Owed : {$480.00} Date Opened ( as reported ) : XX/XX/XXXX Date Reported : XX/XX/XXXX Account Status : Collection / Charge-Off Reporting Bureau XXXX XXXX Failure to Provide Proof of Legal Assignment Southwest Recovery Services is reporting this account as a collection obligation without producing any valid proof of assignment or ownership. Under federal law, a third-party debt collector must be able to demonstrate a lawful chain of assignment from the original creditor to itself before it may lawfully collect or report a debt. Legally sufficient proof requires, at minimum : A bill of sale or assignment agreement Documentation that specifically identifies this account as part of the transfer Proof that Southwest Recovery Services has authority to collect and furnish data to consumer reporting agencies A copy of a billing statement, invoice, account summary, or payment ledger from the original creditor is NOT legally sufficient. Such documents do not establish ownership or assignment, and any party can create or reproduce them. Courts and regulators require actual assignment contracts, not generic account documents. Fair Credit Reporting Act ( FCRA ) Violations By continuing to report this collection account without proof of assignment, Southwest Recovery Services is violating, but not limited to : 15 U.S.C. 1681s-2 ( a ) ( 1 ) ( A ) Furnishing information that is inaccurate, incomplete, or materially misleading. 15 U.S.C. 1681s-2 ( b ) Failure to conduct a reasonable investigation and verify legal authority after dispute. 15 U.S.C. 1681e ( b ) Failure to maintain reasonable procedures to assure maximum possible accuracy. Without proof of lawful assignment, Southwest Recovery Services has no permissible purpose to report this tradeline. Demand for Relief I hereby demand that Southwest Recovery Services : Immediately delete this tradeline from all consumer reporting agencies, including XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX Absent production of valid assignment documentation, continued reporting constitutes willful noncompliance with federal law. This complaint is being submitted to the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau ( CFPB ) for regulatory review and enforcement. Please provide a written response within the CFPB-mandated response timeframe.

I made my payments in good faith and on time. As of XX/XX/XXXX, my remaining balance was approximately {$2400.00}. The explanation I received led me to believe that maintaining on-time payments was sufficient to avoid interest. Had I understood that interest was accruing in the background and would be added retroactively if the balance was not paid in full by a specific date, I would have acted differently.

Attempts to Resolve the Issue I contacted Synchrony Bank directly and attempted to resolve this matter through their hardship department, requesting a goodwill or promotional interest adjustment due to the lack of clear disclosure and my good-faith payment history. I am filing this complaint against US Collections West , Inc. for unlawfully reporting an alleged collection account that I do not recognize and for failing to comply with federal debt collection and credit reporting laws. This account appeared on my credit report without any prior written notice, communication, or legally required disclosure of my right to dispute, in direct violation of FDCPA 1692g ( a ). I never received a dunning letter, written notice of debt, itemized statement, or any documentation explaining the nature, origin, or calculation of this alleged balance before US Collections West began reporting it to the credit bureaus. After disputing the account, US Collections West failed to provide lawful validation and continues to furnish this account as accurate despite possessing no verifiable evidence. Proper debt validation requires the original signed lease or agreement, a complete rent ledger, move-out accounting, itemized damages, proof of charges, documentation of any alleged balance owed, and clear chain of assignment establishing US Collections Wests legal authority to collect. None of this has been provided. Reporting a rental or property-related debt without documentation is inherently unreliable and violates FCRA 1681e ( b ), 1681i ( a ), and 1681s-2 ( b ), as well as Metro-2 accuracy and completeness requirements. US Collections West has a documented history of consumer complaints and regulatory scrutiny for aggressive collection practices, failure to validate debts, and continued reporting of disputed accounts without proof. Furnishing an unverified debt constitutes false representation under FDCPA 1692e, unfair collection practices under 1692f, and a failure to conduct a reasonable investigation under the FCRA. I am fully aware of my consumer rights and what constitutes lawful validation. Continued reporting of this account without evidence demonstrates reckless disregard for federal law.

I am submitting this feedback because the companys response does not resolve my complaint, does not provide legally sufficient validation of the alleged debt, and does not justify the continued reporting of an account that does not belong to me. Because my previous CFPB complaint, Case Number XXXX, was closed without correcting the inaccurate reporting or requiring proof of liability, I am explicitly stating that I am creating a new CFPB case to ensure this matter receives proper review and enforcement. 

The core issue remains unchanged : I do not own this account, I did not authorize it, and the company has not provided proof that I am legally responsible for the alleged debt. Despite multiple disputes, an FTC identity theft report, and prior CFPB involvement, Fair Collections & Outsourcing ( FCO ) continues to report this account without producing documentation that establishes my liability. 

In its response, FCO claims that the account was placed with them, that a verification of debt was mailed, and that the account allegedly includes a signed lease agreement. However, none of these documents have been provided to me. Simply stating that documents exist is not the same as producing them. A furnisher can not satisfy its obligations by describing evidence without disclosing it, especially when the consumer has disputed the account as not theirs and has filed an FTC identity theft report. 

The company further requests that I provide proof of residency during the time in question. This request is improper and does not establish debt ownership. Residency does not prove that a consumer opened, authorized, or incurred a debt. Consumers are not required to reconstruct historical residency records to disprove an obligation they never incurred. This request improperly shifts the burden of proof from the furnisher to the consumer and does not comply with credit reporting standards. 

FCO also asserts that it possesses a signed lease agreement but refuses to provide it, claiming that certain agreements are confidential. This position is misleading. A document allegedly signed by me and used to establish my liability is not a confidential agreement between FCO and its client ; it is purported evidence of consumer responsibility. If such a document exists, it must be disclosed during validation and dispute processes. Withholding the alleged lease while continuing to report the debt is not compliant with consumer protection requirements. 

The response further fails to explain how the account was verified during the credit bureau dispute process. There is no description of what documents were reviewed, who reviewed them, or how FCO confirmed that I am the correct consumer. Without a clear explanation of the method of verification, the response does not demonstrate that a reasonable investigation occurred. Generic statements that the account was verified are insufficient. 

I filed an FTC Identity Theft Report because this account is not mine. Filing an FTC report is a formal declaration that the account is fraudulent or misattributed. Once an identity theft claim is raised, the furnisher must substantiate the debt with original documentation proving the consumers responsibility. Instead of providing proof, FCO has continued reporting the account and has requested consumer-supplied documents unrelated to debt ownership. This approach is inconsistent with identity theft protections and does not satisfy the furnishers obligations. 

The response also does not address why the account was reported initially without validation, why it continued to be reported after multiple disputes, or why the alleged documentation was not produced when first requested. Because CFPB Case XXXX was closed without resolving these issues, I am now creating a new CFPB case to pursue a substantive outcome. Closing a complaint does not convert unverified information into verified information, nor does it relieve the furnisher of its duty to ensure accuracy. The continued reporting of this account without proof remains inaccurate regardless of the procedural status of prior cases. 

This feedback is submitted to clearly document the following facts : I do not own the account reported by FCO I filed an FTC Identity Theft Report FCO has not produced original documentation proving liability Residency does not establish debt ownership Claiming a signed lease without producing it is not validation The method of verification has not been disclosed Prior CFPB Case XXXX was closed without resolution A new CFPB case is being created due to ongoing inaccurate reporting I am requesting that the CFPB take this feedback into account when reviewing the new complaint related to this matter. In conclusion, the companys response does not resolve the complaint, does not validate the debt, and does not justify continued reporting. Background : The subject property was originally owned by my grandmother [ Grandmother 's Name ], the original borrower. Upon her death, her husband, XXXX XXXX, became the sole owner of the property and the XXXX in XXXX by operation of law ( Tenants by the Entirety ). The Dispute : Wells Fargo has repeatedly refused to recognize this trust transfer as an exempt transaction under the Garn-St. Germain Depository Institutions Act of 1982. The banks stated " final decision '' is that because XXXX XXXX was not the " original borrower '' on the promissory note, he does not enjoy the protections of the Act.

Recognition of Successor Status ( 12 C.F.R. 1024.31 ) : Under Regulation X, a person who acquires property via the death of a spouse or through " devise, descent, or operation of law on the death of a joint tenant '' is a XXXX in XXXX. Once confirmed, a successor must be treated as a " borrower '' for the purposes of mortgage servicing and federal consumer protections. 
XXXX. Exempt Transfer ( 12 U.S.C. 1701j-3 ( d ) ( 3 ) ) : The initial transfer to XXXX XXXX was exempt from acceleration because it occurred by operation of law upon the death of a tenant by the entirety. 
XXXX. Trust Transfer Protection ( 12 U.S.C. 1701j-3 ( d ) ( 8 ) ) : As a confirmed successor holding the legal status of a " borrower, '' XXXX XXXX subsequent transfer into an inter vivos trust is an exempt transaction. The Act prohibits a lender from exercising a due-on-sale clause for " a transfer into an inter vivos trust in which the borrower is and remains a beneficiary. '' 4. Failure to Respond to Notice of Error ( 12 C.F.R. 1024.35 ) : I have sent multiple Notices of Error. The bank continues to rely on a pedantic " original borrower '' argument that has been explicitly superseded by the CFPBs 2016 XXXX in XXXX rules, which mandate that successors be afforded the same rights as the original signer of the note.

2. Accept the transfer of the property into the XXXX XXXX XXXX as a protected, non-triggering event under federal law.

Elements include : Filing without proper standing or authority Lack of good faith basis for the claim Malicious or spiteful intent Resulting harm to the defendant This tort is particularly relevant when lenders file foreclosure without proper ownership documentation or with knowledge of chain-of-title defects.

Consumer complaint narrative:
On XX/XX/year>, my phone was stolen. During the period in which the thief had access to my device and accounts, my PayPal account was compromised and a PayPal debit card was fraudulently opened and digitally provisioned without my authorization. 

Once I regained access to my email account, I noticed ( and have attached ) an email from PayPal indicating that the PayPal debit card was added to XXXX XXXX during the same timeframe that my phone was stolen and under the thiefs control. I did not request the debit card, did not authorize it to be added to XXXX XXXX, and did not authorize any transactions made using it. 

Using the digitally provisioned PayPal debit card, the thief made unauthorized transactions, including a {$500.00} transaction at XXXX on XX/XX/year>. 

I later physically received the PayPal debit card by mail and still have it in my possession. The disputed transaction occurred before I had possession of or access to the physical card, confirming that the transaction was conducted digitally using the compromised device and PayPal app. 

I promptly reported the unauthorized activity to PayPal, filed a police report, and submitted an FTC Identity Theft affidavit. Despite this, PayPal denied both my original dispute and my appeal. 

In its written denial, PayPal stated that the claim was denied because : - Personal payments were received into the PayPal account shortly before the disputed transaction - The transaction did not exceed the available account balance - The account was accessed using login information consistent with preceding account access - These factors allegedly indicated account holder knowledge and authorization This reasoning is flawed and inconsistent with identity theft protections. 

First, the PayPal debit card itself was opened and digitally provisioned without my authorization. PayPal did not meaningfully address or investigate the unauthorized creation and XXXX XXXX attachment of the debit card during a known account compromise. 

Second, consistent logins do not establish authorization. A stolen phone with saved credentials, session persistence, or biometric/passcode access will naturally generate logins that appear consistent. Treating this as proof of authorization ignores well-established identity theft and device compromise scenarios. 

Third, PayPals reliance on account balance awareness or inbound payments is speculative. Knowledge of an account balance does not prove authorization when an account has been taken over by a third party. 

Finally, PayPal failed to account for the following undisputed facts : - The debit card was created and added to XXXXXXXX XXXX without my consent- The transaction occurred digitally during the period my phone was stolen - I did not possess or control the physical debit card at the time - Police and FTC identity theft reports were filed PayPal concluded that the transaction was processed correctly without demonstrating that I authorized the debit card issuance, the Apple Pay provisioning, or the transaction itself.

I respectfully request that the CFPB review PayPals handling of this dispute, including whether its investigation complied with consumer protection requirements for unauthorized electronic fund transfers and whether its denial improperly relied on assumptions rather than affirmative evidence of authorization.

The bag was returned and delivered appropriately. The merchant denied receiving the bag.The merchant failed to comply with multiple consumer protection and billing requirements applicable to loss claims and disputed charges.

Despite asserting that I was responsible for the value of the item, the merchant did not provide the information necessary to validate the amount claimed. I formally requested documentation to substantiate the quoted {$1800.00} figure, including valuation methodology, depreciation, prior rentals, condition history, and any insurance claim information. The merchant failed to provide this information and nonetheless proceeded with charging and collection activity.

This conduct violates the following consumer protection standards : Fair Credit Billing Act ( FCBA ) - The merchant continued billing my account after I disputed the charge and requested clarification. A billing error under the FCBA includes charges for incorrect amounts and charges not adequately explained. The merchant failed to reasonably investigate or substantiate the disputed amount before charging {$610.00} after quoting {$1800.00}.

Failure to Validate a Disputed Debt - Once a consumer requests validation of a claimed amount, the creditor must provide sufficient detail to substantiate how the amount was calculated. Merely referencing internal terms and conditions is insufficient. The merchant did not explain how the {$1800.00} amount was derived, preventing me from determining whether the charge was accurate or reasonable.

Fair Debt Collection Practices Act ( FDCPA ) - After partially charging my account, the merchant sold an alleged balance to a collection agency in the amount of {$2100.00}. This amount exceeds the quoted settlement and does not account for the {$610.00} already collected. Representing an incorrect or inflated balance constitutes a false or misleading representation of the amount of a debt and an unfair collection practice under the FDCPA.

Unfair, Deceptive, or Abusive Acts or Practices ( UDAAP ) - The merchant engaged in unfair and deceptive practices by withholding material information needed to evaluate the charge, charging during an unresolved dispute, and selling an inaccurate balance to collections. Consumers can not be expected to assess or pay charges that are not transparently calculated or validated.

Because the merchant failed to substantiate the loss valuation, improperly charged my account during a dispute, and sold an inflated and inaccurate balance to collections, the alleged debt is invalid. I am requesting correction of the charges, withdrawal of the collection account, and confirmation that no adverse credit reporting will occur.

These delays were not caused by insufficient funds, incorrect bank information, or any failure on my part, but by the servicers own payment processing system.

I formally disputed the inaccurate reporting directly with the mortgage servicer and provided documentation, including proof of my correct bank information. The servicer denied my dispute solely based on the date the payment posted and failed to investigate the payment system failure that caused the delay. 



Under the Fair Credit Reporting Act, furnishers are required to ensure that information reported to the credit bureaus is accurate and complete. Reporting payments as late without considering documented system errors that prevented timely payment is inaccurate. 



I am requesting that the mortgage servicer : Correct or remove the inaccurate late payment reporting from all credit bureaus Confirm in writing that my credit reports have been updated to reflect accurate payment history I have attached documentation supporting my attempts to pay, proof of my bank information, and the servicers dispute denial.

Issue: Problem with additional add-on products or services
Consumer complaint narrative:
In late 2025, I used Affirm to finance a patio furniture purchase from XXXX. I knowingly made the furniture purchase ; however, I did not knowingly authorize or consent to a warranty/insurance add-on that was bundled into the Affirm loan and charged at an amount comparable toor exceedingthe cost of the furniture itself. 

After reviewing my payment schedule and charges, I discovered the warranty/insurance cost and immediately contacted Affirm to dispute the add-on as unauthorized. This dispute was not about identity theft and not about the furniture purchase itself, but about a fraudulent or improperly disclosed add-on. 

First Attempt During my first call with Affirm, I explained that the warranty/insurance was not authorized. The representative indicated the dispute would be filed. I later learned that this dispute was never properly submitted or documented on Affirms end.

Second Attempt I contacted Affirm again to follow up. During this call, I again explained that this was not identity theft, but an unauthorized add-on. Neither the representative nor the manager I spoke with advised that an affidavit was required. I later discovered that the case had not progressed properly. 

Affidavit Confusion On a subsequent interaction, an Affirm representative incorrectly instructed me to complete an affidavit by selecting an identity theft option, despite my repeated explanation that no identity theft had occurred. I had difficulty locating the affidavit form and had to make multiple calls due to unclear and incomplete instructions. The affidavit selection was made solely based on Affirms guidance, not because it accurately reflected my claim. 

Improper Investigation and Denial Affirm denied my claim after conducting an investigation that focused on IP address matching, device usage, and prior purchasing patternsfactors relevant to identity verification but not relevant to whether I affirmatively consented to an optional warranty/insurance product. Affirm did not provide documentation showing clear, separate, and affirmative authorization of the add-on.

Record Correction and Second Review I formally corrected the record in writing, explaining that the dispute involved an unauthorized add-on and not identity theft. I requested that Affirm reopen the case under the correct dispute category and provide proof of consent. Affirm conducted another review but again denied the claim without addressing the authorization issue or providing proof of consent.

Final Denial and Credit Reporting Threat Affirm issued a final denial stating I am responsible for the loan and that all payment information would continue to be reported to credit bureaus, despite the unresolved billing dispute. Affirm has never produced evidence of affirmative consent to the warranty/insurance, nor acknowledged the procedural failures in handling the dispute. 

Ongoing Harm As a result, I remain charged for an unauthorized add-on, face ongoing payment obligations, and am concerned about inaccurate credit reporting. I am seeking regulatory assistance to require Affirm to properly investigate this billing error, produce proof of consent, and correct the disputed charges.

This complaint follows prior CFPB complaint # XXXX, submitted on XX/XX/year>. In its response dated XX/XX/year>, Experian did not verify the account, did not provide supporting documentation, and did not delete the account. Instead, Experian issued a generic response suggesting that I may have been a victim of fraud and directed me toward fraud and identity theft resources. 

This response was legally insufficient and did not meet the requirements of a reasonable reinvestigation under the Fair Credit Reporting Act ( 15 U.S.C. 1681i ). 

To be absolutely clear, I have not alleged identity theft, have not filed an FTC identity theft affidavit, and have not claimed fraud in connection with this account. My dispute concerns the accuracy and legal verifiability of the reporting. Experians decision to redirect this matter into a fraud or identity theft framework appears to be a mischaracterization of my dispute and functions as a stall tactic rather than a lawful reinvestigation. 

Directing a consumer to file an identity theft or fraud report when no theft has been alleged improperly shifts the burden of investigation away from the consumer reporting agency and onto the consumer. The Fair Credit Reporting Act requires the credit bureau to conduct a reasonable reinvestigation when inaccuracies are disputed. It does not permit a credit bureau to avoid this obligation by reframing an accuracy dispute as a potential fraud claim. 

If Experian genuinely believes fraud is possible, continued reporting of the account without deletion or proper verification is reckless and inconsistent with the FCRAs accuracy requirements under 15 U.S.C. 1681e ( b ). A consumer reporting agency can not simultaneously question the validity of an account while continuing to report it as verified and accurate.

Issue: Problem caused by your funds being low
Consumer complaint narrative:
Product : Savings account Company : Wells Fargo Bank , N.A . 

What happened? 

Wells Fargo assessed monthly maintenance fees on my Way2Save savings account despite the account meeting the disclosed minimum balance requirement.

The Wells Fargo mobile app displayed my account balance as {$300.00} as of XX/XX/XXXX, and the balance remained at or above {$300.00} at statement end. 

Wells Fargo nonetheless charged $ XXXX monthly service fees on XX/XX/XXXX and XX/XX/XXXX. 

After I contacted Wells Fargo by phone on XX/XX/XXXX, both fees were reversed as erroneous ( + {$10.00} total ). 

Wells Fargo did not provide a written or clear explanation for why the fees were assessed or what balance methodology was applied. 

The account disclosure states that the $ XXXX  monthly service fee applies when the balance is less than {$300.00}. The mobile app prominently displays balances to consumers without clearly indicating that those balances may not be used for fee assessment.

Why is this a problem?

This practice is deceptive and unfair to a reasonable consumer.

A reasonable consumer would rely on the balance displayed in Wells Fargos app to determine whether the disclosed {$300.00} minimum balance requirement has been met. 

If Wells Fargo instead uses a different internal metric ( such as a minimum daily balance during the statement period, ledger balance timing, or fee-first posting logic ), that methodology was not clearly or conspicuously disclosed at the time the fees were assessed. 

Charging fees under these circumstances causes avoidable financial harm, requires consumers to spend time disputing charges, and is not reasonably avoidable when the banks own interface presents misleading balance information. 

The fact that Wells Fargo reversed both fees upon contact indicates the charges were improperly applied or inconsistently assessed, reinforcing concerns about systemic misapplication rather than isolated error.

I am concerned this practice may be systemic and affecting other consumers who reasonably rely on app-displayed balances to avoid fees.

This correspondence is in response to your letter denying responsibility for the undisclosed and unsafe conditions present in the XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX ( XXXX : XXXX ) sold in XX/XX/XXXX. 

While I acknowledge that the XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX Contract was executed and that the vehicle was sold as-is, your position materially misstates Texas XXXX and mischaracterizes the conditions identified after delivery. 

An as-is sale does not permit the sale of an unsafe or unroadworthy vehicle, nor does it shield a dealer from liability arising from misrepresentation, omission of material facts, or violations of the Texas Deceptive Trade Practices Act ( DTPA ). 

Specifically : The absence of rear brake pads is not a cosmetic issue, routine maintenance item, or normal wear and tear. Brakes are a primary safety system, and a vehicle sold without functional rear braking components is unsafe and unroadworthy at the time of sale. 

Coolant system leakage and windshield washer reservoir leakage are not cosmetic concerns. These conditions pose risks of engine overheating and impaired visibility and directly impact vehicle safety. 

The absence of a wheel-lock key materially interferes with the ability to safely service the vehicle and constitutes a missing essential accessory. 

An inoperative sunroof constitutes a material feature failure that was not disclosed prior to sale. 

Your assertion that the vehicle passed inspection appears to reference emissions inspection only. An emissions inspection does not constitute a safety inspection, and any implication that the vehicle was roadworthy based solely on emissions compliance is misleading. 

These conditions were identified shortly after delivery and are consistent with pre-existing defects. Brake pads do not deteriorate to non-existence within weeks of ordinary post-sale use. Responsibility can not be shifted to the buyer by characterizing safety defects as post-delivery issues. 

This letter constitutes formal notice under the Texas Deceptive Trade Practices Act, based on misrepresentation of the vehicles condition, failure to disclose material safety defects, and the sale of an unsafe product. Remedies available under Texas law include repair, replacement, rescission of the transaction, damages, and attorneys fees.

On XX/XX/XXXX, I purchased a score on XXXX via PayPal. In the checkout process, I never saw anything about a subscription. I certainly never added it to my cart- I can bet my life on that. Just like I would if someone stole my credit card and made an unauthorized purchase, I went to PayPal because XXXX made an unauthorized purchase. I submitted my story, they supposedly contacted XXXX for more info, and I just learned today that they decided in XXXX 's favor. 

Here is my problem : I don't have a screen recording of my checkout process. Nobody expects these problems. So, I can't prove I didn't miss something obvious in the checkout process. I can't even prove I didn't intentionally want a subscription and then changed my mind. But, here is the thing... when PayPal decided against me I went looking for ways to warn people off of XXXX. And, I found that they are well-known for these scams. It is all over XXXX. It is all over XXXX. Go look! So, this isn't the one-off report of someone who changed their mind and doesn't want to pay for something they signed up for. Lots of people experience this scam, and PayPal does NOTHING. Unlike what credit card companies do to protect their customers, PayPal is complicit with these scams. How can they possibly decide in XXXX 's favor when the internet is filled with reports that this company scams people? And, PayPal never asked for additional information from me. After talking to XXXX, they are suddenly 100 % sure that it is my fault. After all, why not take the word of a company ( XXXX ) with such a stellar reputation - even on this particular complaint? 

XXXX is a predatory scam. But, I'm here to report PayPal for not caring whether scammers use their platform to extract money from people 's bank accounts - as long as they still get their cut of the transaction. I doubt anyone will step in to make this right. I'm too small of a fish, and nobody is shutting down PayPal. But, I guess I'm at the point where the federal government is my only hope for justice. It isn't like I can sue them ( XXXX  or Paypal ) for {$65.00}, so I guess I'm just screwed. 

I generally consider myself to be a pretty careful person on the internet. When I have to buy from sites that are sketchy ( which I try to avoid ), I've used PayPal before to avoid giving those sites my credit card. I thought they were protection, I thought they had my back. Not only did PayPal allow the start of a subscription without my consent or verification, they did not even give me a reason for why they denied my complaint! I would have been better off giving my credit card, because at least the credit card companies will reverse a charge when there has been fraud. 
Going forward, I'll be using one of those virtual credit card services - I guess. I can make a dedicated card, and set a spending limit. Until PayPal gets scolded for this behavior, I suggest everyone stop using them for purchases. There is no guarantee you won't wind up with a subscription, a charge you didn't authorize, and no recourse whatsoever. 

Here is my last argument : I'm in my late thirties. I'm a web developer. No disabilities. My vision is good. I'm attentive to scams. I can make mistakes. But, if I ended up with a subscription I didn't authorize, and the internet is filled with similar stories, how much more is this predatory for people as they get older or have disabilities? How horrible is PayPal to blindly support these scammers, just because they get a cut? I want to associate with brands that ban companies for predatory behavior, at least until they correct their ways. Then, I could trust that if I pay via PayPal I am safe. Were PayPal to have made it right, I would say that I using PayPal MAY be safe - because they still allowed the subscription to start without my consent in the first place. But, since PayPal was complicit in the scam, I have to say that they aren't safe, they aren't neutral, they are unsafe.

Issue: Attempts to collect debt not owed
Consumer complaint narrative: I am submitting this complaint regarding a civil lawsuit filed against me by ZWICKER & ASSOCIATES, P.C., acting on behalf of XXXX XXXX XXXXXXXX XXXX amounting of {$14000.00} and/or any other amount. I am not the debtor in this matter. The account and debt being used as the basis for this legal action resulted from the fraudulent use of my personal identifying information by an unknown individual, without my knowledge, authorization, or consent. This situation is the result of identity-related fraud. I did not apply for, authorize, or benefit from the alleged account or any related transactions. Despite this, I am being subjected to collection efforts and a civil case for an obligation that does not belong to me. This has caused severe emotional distress, anxiety, and disruption to my financial and personal life. Being forced to defend myself in court for a fraudulent debt is overwhelming and unjust. The continued pursuit of this debt violates multiple consumer protection laws. Under the Fair Debt Collection Practices Act ( FDCPA ), 15 U.S.C. 1692 et seq., debt collectors are prohibited from attempting to collect debts that are not owed and from using false, deceptive, or misleading representations. Proceeding with a civil lawsuit against an individual who is not the true debtor constitutes an unfair and abusive collection practice. Additionally, the Fair Credit Reporting Act ( FCRA ), 15 U.S.C. 1681 et seq., requires that information furnished and reported about consumers be accurate and properly investigated. Reporting or relying on a debt created through identity theft fails the requirement of maximum possible accuracy and exposes consumers to serious harm. Victims of fraud should not be subjected to legal or financial consequences for debts they did not incur. Florida law further protects victims of identity theft. Florida Statutes 817.568 prohibits the criminal use of personal identification information and makes clear that fraudulent use of another persons identity for financial purposes is unlawful. Florida Statutes 501.98 provides protections for identity theft victims and establishes that individuals are not responsible for debts incurred through fraudulent means. The continued legal and collection actions in this case disregard these protections. I am now taking all necessary legal steps to resolve this error, stop the misuse of my identity, and correct the inaccurate records associated with this fraudulent debt. I am filing a police report. I am seeking relief from ongoing harm and requesting that all collection activity and legal action related to this matter cease immediately. No consumer should be forced to defend themselves against a lawsuit based on fraud. I am asking the CFPB to intervene, review this matter, and ensure compliance with the FDCPA, FCRA, and applicable Florida laws. I request that this fraudulent account and all related collection efforts be halted, that my consumer rights be enforced, and that appropriate corrective action be taken to prevent further harm.
